text:
tara: Quick sync: proposing a runtime backoff heuristic for low-bit paths instead of a global shim. idea is per-request decide fp8->int8/4bit fallback based on recent token-level confidence.

jamal: sounds promising. what's the trigger window? last N tokens or sliding time window?

tara: sliding window by tokens, default 64, with exponential decay. if avg logprob drops below threshold -> try higher-precision fallback for next K tokens.

mira: how do we avoid oscillation? repeated flips will kill perf.

tara: include hysteresis: min-duration for a decision (500ms) and a cooldown (5s). also prefer increasing precision only, never lower until cooldown expires.

ryan: telemetry wise we need tags: `backoff_decision`, `backoff_reason`, and `backoff_duration`. add sampling to avoid noise.

jamal: ops note: we need a canary for this just like for shim removal. propose enabling for 2% traffic, run for 48h, compare `degradation_score` and `cpu_gpu_util`.

ops-bot: scheduled canary window created: 2025-06-10 00:00 UTC -> 2025-06-12 00:00 UTC. will notify on enable.

mira: QA ask: add prompts that stress numeric stability (long math, long context). also capture token-level logprob traces for postmortem.

tara: will draft a PR with config knobs and default values. aim to land experiment behind `runtime.backoff.enabled` flag.

jamal: I'll wire dashboard panels and alert gates. if p50 latency up > 10% or `regression_score` > 0.02 -> auto rollback.

mira: ok. team sync Friday 11am PT to review PR and canary plan. thanks.
